subject.title: [Bug]: web_fetch reports exact-size responses as truncated

question: Which exact-cap contract should `readResponseText` use before another fix PR lands for this issue?
rationale: Current behavior is source-proven wrong for a real exact-size response, but a naive equality removal or one-read lookahead can weaken the helper's bounded-read availability guarantee; the repository member close comment already asked for an explicit contract or real proof.

options.title: Use content-length or explicit bounded overread
options.body: Define a narrow completion rule, such as trusting finite `Content-Length <= maxBytes` or a bounded overread/timeout, then require tests for exact, overflow, empty-chunk, and stalled-stream cases.

options.title: Require more real-response proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open until a maintainer accepts the closed duplicate's httpbin proof or asks for additional live evidence on current main.

options.title: Keep truncation-conservative behavior
options.body: Close or downgrade the report if maintainers prefer the current false-positive warning over any additional read/contract complexity at the byte cap.

recommendation.title: Use content-length or explicit bounded overread
recommendation.body: Define a narrow completion rule, such as trusting finite `Content-Length <= maxBytes` or a bounded overread/timeout, then require tests for exact, overflow, empty-chunk, and stalled-stream cases.

likelyOwner.reason: He already made the same-cluster contract/proof decision on the prior PR and has recent history in the bounded response helper.
